title: Procedural Graphs: Self-Evolving Execution Structures for LLM Agents

numericClaims.quote: PG ranks first or joint first in 21 of 24 model–benchmark settings.
Compared with the strongest baseline in each setting, PG records 19 wins, two ties, and three losses (one-sided exact binomial sign test excluding ties, 𝑝 = 4.3 × 10−4).

Its largest margins are on BFCL v3 with Gemini 3.5 Flash (67.00% vs. 58.00%, +9.00 points), GDPval with Gemini 3.1 Pro (78.78 vs. 71.37, +7.41 points), and 𝜏-bench with the same model (80.00% vs. 73.04%, +6.96 points).

It raises survival from 44.0% to 58.0% for Claude Sonnet 4.6, from 6.0% to 34.0% for Gemini 3.1 Pro, and from 26.0% to 40.0% for Grok 4.1 Fast, where it also delivers the best average enterprise score ($39.62M).
It issues 18.94 tool calls per month, which the graph reduces to 12.53 while improving the average enterprise score.
Average capital raised is $0.00M for the Flash baseline, compared with $9.39M for PG-guided Flash and $30.11M for PG-guided Grok 4.1 Fast.

On HotpotQA, Mode 5 (Scratch + Online Evolution) achieves the highest performance across all configurations, scoring 78.79% Ans F1 and 66.30% Ans EM (gains of 7.58 F1 points and 7.50 EM points over the unguided baseline).
The iterative configuration (Mode 3), which combines fresh execution feedback with validation gating, recovers to 92.86%, a gain of 33.93 points over the expert initialization.

Round 1 discovers the sequential backbone that guides the agent to audit cash and forecast runway before a financing decision, producing the largest single jump (0.0% → 45.0% validation survival); Round 2 adds recall_notes to reuse the notes saved by the Round 1 graph and lifts survival to 80.0%, with tool usage falling from 17.23 to 3.08 calls per month relative to the unguided baseline.

The returned graph reaches 85.0% test survival against the baseline’s 0.0% (Fisher’s exact 𝑝 = 2.6 × 10−8), while the best single round observed during the search reached 95.0%; we report the former, since quoting the latter would amount to selecting on the test set.
Localization reduces total tokens relative to full-graph generative guidance on all three benchmarks: by 70.9% on ALFWorld, 18.1% on GDPval, and 14.8% on MultiChallenge.
Online guidance uses the ℎ=2 hop neighborhood of the localized node and a recent trajectory window of 𝑤=3.

questions.question: What analogy does the Procedural Graph draw with knowledge graphs?
questions.answer: Just as a knowledge graph organizes factual knowledge into (entity, relation, entity) triplets for what-is questions, a Procedural Graph organizes procedural knowledge into (procedure, relation, procedure) triplets for what-to-do questions.

questions.question: What three textual attribute fields does each edge carry in the implementation?
questions.answer: condition, guidance, and pitfalls — describing when the transition applies, how to proceed, and what to avoid.

questions.question: Which seven benchmarks are used to evaluate procedural reasoning?
questions.answer: HotpotQA (multi-hop QA with search tools), MultiChallenge (instruction retention across multi-turn conversations), GDPval (open-ended professional tasks scored against expert rubrics), ALFWorld (embodied household tasks), 𝜏-bench (policy-compliant tool use), BFCL (multi-turn function calling), and EnterpriseArena (long-horizon financial decision-making).

questions.question: Which four LLMs are evaluated, and what decoding is used?
questions.answer: Claude Sonnet 4.6, Gemini 3.1 Pro, Gemini 3.5 Flash, and Grok 4.1 Fast; all calls use greedy decoding (temperature 0) for reproducibility, and the guidance model and offline refiner share the same underlying LLM as the solver.

questions.question: What are the four steps of the self-evolution loop?
questions.answer: (1) Diagnostic Rollout on a batch of training tasks, (2) Feedback-Driven Mutation producing structured Add/Delete/Update edits, (3) Validation Gating on a held-out validation set, and (4) Rejection Memory as a Safeguard, which logs rejected candidates as negative evidence for the refiner.

questions.question: What hop neighborhood and trajectory window size are used for online guidance?
questions.answer: The h = 2 hop neighborhood of the localized node and a recent trajectory window of w = 3 steps.

questions.question: What is the maximum horizon of EnterpriseArena and how many scheduled crises does it include?
questions.answer: The agent makes monthly financial decisions over up to 132 months under strict liquidity constraints, with three scheduled crises that are not disclosed to the agent.

questions.question: How does PG change survival for Claude Sonnet 4.6 on EnterpriseArena?
questions.answer: It raises survival from 44.0% to 58.0%; PG achieves the highest or joint-highest full-horizon survival and the longest average lifespan across all four LLMs.

questions.question: Which PG construction mode performs best on HotpotQA and with what scores?
questions.answer: Mode 5 (Scratch + Online Evolution): 78.79% Ans F1 and 66.30% Ans EM — the highest across all configurations, gains of 7.58 F1 and 7.50 EM points over the unguided baseline.

questions.question: What happens on MultiChallenge when using the hand-crafted expert graph, and does the evolution loop recover?
questions.answer: Mode 1 (hand-crafted expert) lowers success from 87.50% to 58.93%; a single offline update (Mode 2) lowers it further to 53.57%; the iterative Mode 3 (Expert + Online Evolution) recovers to 92.86%, a gain of 33.93 points over expert initialization.

questions.question: In the efficiency ablation (Table 3), which graph configuration achieves the highest performance, and by how much does it beat the best alternative?
questions.answer: Subgraph + generative guidance (localized), scoring 89.31 on MultiChallenge, 63.99 on GDPval, and 81.53 on ALFWorld — exceeding the best alternative in each setting, including the no-graph baseline, by 2.0, 6.8, and 9.0 points respectively.

questions.question: Across the main comparison, how many wins, ties, and losses does PG record against the strongest baseline per setting?
questions.answer: 19 wins, two ties, and three losses (one-sided exact binomial sign test excluding ties, p = 4.3 × 10−4), ranking first or joint first in 21 of 24 model–benchmark settings.

questions.question: How many GPU-hours or dollars did the self-evolution loop and evaluation consume?
Does the Procedural Graph still help when the solver is a smaller open-weight model such as an 8B Llama?
How does PG perform on mathematical reasoning benchmarks like GSM8K?

unanswerableNote: Compute cost is never reported; solver transfer (e.g., to small open-weight models) is explicitly left as future work, and no math-reasoning benchmark is among the seven evaluated.
